sn56.49:1.1: “Bhikkhus, suppose that a man would place on Sineru, the king of mountains, seven grains of gravel the size of mung beans.
sn56.49:1.3: which is more: the seven grains of gravel the size of mung beans that have been placed there or Sineru, the king of mountains?”
sn56.49:1.4: “Venerable sir, Sineru, the king of mountains, is more.
sn56.49:1.5: The seven grains of gravel the size of mung beans are trifling.
sn56.49:1.6: Compared to Sineru, the king of mountains, the seven grains of gravel the size of mung beans are not calculable, do not bear comparison, do not amount even to a fraction.”
sn56.49:1.7: “So too, bhikkhus, for a noble disciple, a person accomplished in view who has made the breakthrough, the suffering that has been utterly destroyed and eliminated is more, while that which remains is trifling.
sn56.49:1.8: Compared to the former mass of suffering that has been destroyed and eliminated, the latter is not calculable, does not bear comparison, does not amount even to a fraction, as there is a maximum of seven more lives.
sn56.49:1.9: He is one who understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’
sn56.49:2.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
